description: Our team is working on the Mars Ecological Dome project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
summary: Our project, developed for the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge, is an integrated, multi-layered interactive map designed to help future astronauts navigate and survive on Mars. By combining topographical data, volcanic terrain mapping, and environmental hazard zones from NASA's Mars exploration missions, our guide identifies safe landing sites, optimal travel routes, and potential resource locations. This tool empowers human explorers to plan efficient Marswalks, avoid extreme terrain dangers, and conduct high-value scientific research safely on the Red Planet.
details:
How It Works & Features: Our Martian Survival Map layers multiple datasets—including elevation models, volcanic regions (such as Olympus Mons and Tharsis), and surface conditions—into a unified visual guide for astronauts. Explorers can assess route difficulty, identify scientific points of interest, and locate safe zones.

Tools & Development: Our team utilized NASA planetary datasets for spatial mapping, Canva for visual interface and presentation design, and CapCut for video demonstration. We focused on clear visual hierarchy and accessibility so astronauts can quickly interpret critical survival information during missions.
